top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
top_sast_rules.description: Modifying an object obtained via a user-controlled property name may lead to accidental mutation of the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement proper output encoding based on context (HTML, JavaScript, CSS, URL). Use Content Security Policy and validate input.

top_sast_rules.description: Assigning to a property of a primitive value has no effect and may trigger a runtime error.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement secure coding practices specific to CWE-704. Review OWASP guidelines and CWE documentation for detailed mitigation strategies.

top_sast_rules.description: An assignment to a local variable that is not used later on, or whose value is always overwritten, has no effect.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Remove unused variables that may contain sensitive data. Use static analysis tools to identify unused code. Review code for potential logic errors.

top_sast_rules.description: Assigning a variable to itself has no effect.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Remove dead code through static analysis. Use code coverage tools to identify unreachable code. Implement regular code reviews to eliminate unused functionality.

top_sast_rules.description: Comparing the result of a typeof test against a string other than 'undefined', 'boolean', 'number', 'string', 'object', 'function' or 'symbol' is useless, since this comparison can never succeed.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement secure coding practices specific to CWE-571. Review OWASP guidelines and CWE documentation for detailed mitigation strategies.

top_sast_rules.description: Accessing paths influenced by users can allow an attacker to access unexpected resources.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement secure coding practices specific to CWE-023. Review OWASP guidelines and CWE documentation for detailed mitigation strategies.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')
top_sast_rules.description: Building an XPath expression from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious code by the user.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement path validation using canonical paths. Reject paths containing '../' or similar traversal sequences.

top_sast_rules.description: Deserializing user-controlled data may allow attackers to execute arbitrary code.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Identify deserialization operations on untrusted data without proper validation
top_sast_rules.remediation: Use safe serialization formats like JSON. If complex deserialization is needed, implement strict validation and type checking.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
top_sast_rules.description: Extracting files from a malicious ZIP file, or similar type of archive, without validating that the destination file path is within the destination directory can allow an attacker to unexpectedly gain access to resources.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement path validation using canonical paths. Reject paths containing '../' or similar traversal sequences.

top_sast_rules.description: Allowing writes to arbitrary properties of an object may lead to denial-of-service attacks.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for operations that can consume excessive resources without proper limits or controls
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement resource consumption limits, rate limiting, and proper cleanup mechanisms for all operations.
